## [9.3.0] — 2026-06-20

### Added — CEG-native graph DX: foundation (CIRISPersist#247 + #248)

First cut of the **#249** CEG-native graph DX umbrella (the typed-attestation-graph traversal + emit surface). This cut lays the **emit-side floor** the rest composes on — the derived-key_id fix (#247) and the `emit_attestation` primitive (#248). More cuts (the traversal FFI, enumerators, emit conveniences, replication combinator) follow.

- **#247 — derived-key_id resolver + the alias-vs-derived FK fix.** After CIRISVerify FSD-003, a node's `federation_keys` row is keyed by the **derived** wire key_id `derive_key_id(label, ed25519_pubkey) = "<label>-<fp>"`, while the keystore alias stays the raw label — so any value that must FK to `federation_keys` MUST be the derived id, never the alias. Every federation-tier emit that stamped `signer.current_alias()` as an FK-bound key_id FK-violated on every real node (alias ≠ derived id).
  - **Resolver:** `Engine::local_derived_key_id()` (async; reads the Ed25519 pubkey via the composed `Arc<dyn HardwareSigner>` so it works for software + hardware engines alike) and `LocalSigner::derived_key_id()` / `LocalSigner::ed25519_public_key_bytes()` (sync) — all compute `ciris_verify_core::fedcode::derive_key_id(<alias>, <ed25519 pubkey>)`, reproducing the registered `federation_keys.key_id`.
  - **Fixed FK-write sites (`current_alias()` → derived id):** `Engine::attestation_promote`'s `scrub_key_id` (the named #247 bug — age-assurance / any local→federation promote was unusable on real nodes); `BlobStorage::put_blob_signing`'s holds_bytes `scrub_key_id` and the eviction `emit_withdraws_attestation_helper`'s attester/scrub (same class, surfaced by the withdraws-producer refactor); the eviction sweeper's holds_bytes lookup + `is_local_or_family_key`'s local-identity comparison (consume the derived id so the holds_bytes/withdraws lifecycle is FK-consistent end-to-end).
  - **Left as-is (correctly the alias/label, not an FK):** the `LocalSigner` construction label; the `derive_key_id` `label` argument; the ingest scrub envelope's `scrub_key_id` on `trace_events` (a plain non-FK provenance column). `Engine::local_identity_aggregate`'s published `key_id` is a **separate behavioral concern** (it returns a struct, doesn't FK-crash) tracked for a later cut.
- **#248 — `Engine::emit_attestation(signer, EmitAttestationInput) -> attestation_id`.** THE high-level emit primitive: canonicalize (`ceg_produce_canonicalize`) → SHA-256 → hybrid-sign (`LocalSigner::sign_hybrid`, Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65 bound, the v9.0.0 / CC 5.3.2.4.3.1 PQC mandate) → assemble the 20-field federation-tier `Attestation` → `put_attestation`. **Derives `attesting_key_id` / `scrub_key_id` internally** from the signer (the #247 floor — never a caller alias), so a hand-rolled emit can't FK-violate or forget the PQC half. New `EmitAttestationInput` type (`src/federation/types.rs`, re-exported from `federation`) with an `EmitAttestationInput::with_envelope(type, envelope)` builder (federation cohort_scope default). Consumers (Node / Lens / Registry / Server, and persist's own producer) compose this instead of re-deriving the ~50-line recipe; the local-write → promote two-call shape stays `attestation_upsert_local` + `attestation_promote` (no separate `emit_and_promote` added — `emit_attestation` covers the direct-emit case, the fixed promote covers local→federation).
- **Refactored persist's own withdraws producer onto the primitive.** `Engine::emit_withdraws_attestation` (the eviction-sweeper producer) now composes `emit_attestation` instead of hand-rolling canonicalize→sign→assemble→`put_attestation` — proving the primitive subsumes the hand-roll and inheriting the #247 derived-key_id floor for free.
- **FFI:** `PyEngine.emit_attestation(input_json) -> attestation_id` (uses the engine's configured local signer, mirroring `attestation_promote`'s engine reconstruction; raises `PyValueError` on JSON decode / missing-PQC-signer / backend error). In a clearly-labeled `#247 + #248 CEG-DX foundation` FFI section so later #249 cuts minimize merge surface.
- **Backend + FFI parity** (the fix + emit are backend-agnostic — `emit_attestation` composes `put_attestation`, which all backends implement; verified on sqlite + live Postgres). Test fixtures across the blob / eviction / takedown / self-at-login surface were updated to the **real-node shape** (register the `federation_keys` row under the derived id) — the assumption #247 exists to kill.

### Added — Cut A (FFI-expose existing graph readers) + Cut B (enumerators + add_community_member)

- **Cut A — FFI exposure (#249).** Thin pyo3 wrappers over existing pub Rust readers (zero new Rust logic), unblocking the KMP/Python UI (ex-#104 `PERSIST_DELEGATES_TO`): `lookup_community_json`, `list_communities_for_member_json`, `list_{families,communities}_for_member_active_json` (the revocation-folded variants), `list_{family,community}_membership_revocations_for_json`, `is_named_moderator_json`, `is_owner_bound_json`, `duty_holders_for_community_json`, `duty_holders_for_content_json` (4-arg: `content_sha256, community_id, duty`).
- **Cut B — read-side enumerators + incremental roster grow (#249).** The enumeration companions of existing predicates / forward-only walks:
  - **`active_community_members` / `active_family_members`** — roster MINUS effective (`effective_at <= now`) revocations; the subtraction is **factored** into one shared `federation::removed_key_ids_at` that `community_dek::resolve_community_members` now also composes (not forked).
  - **`admission::reachable_under_scope(issuer, target, scope, max_depth)`** — the **general scoped-delegation reachability primitive** (the by-construction load-bearing walk every delegated-duty reader specializes); a **thin `pub` wrapper** over the previously-private `issuer_reaches_target_via_scoped_delegation` with **zero change** to the ⊆-attenuation / `sub_delegation`-gated / `withdraws`-aware / depth-cap semantics.
  - **`admission::moderators_of(community, duty)`** — full named-moderator set (owner-bound roots ∪ live `duty`-scoped delegated reach); `k ∈ moderators_of ⟺ is_named_moderator(k)`.
  - **`admission::owner_bindings_of(key)`** (the user anchors) + **`owner_binding_chain(key)`** (the audit path) — enumerators over the `is_owner_bound` predicate.
  - **`delegations_to(key)`** — inbound `delegates_to` edges ("who delegated TO me"), reverse of the forward-only delegation graph.
  - **`add_community_member(community, member)`** — incremental roster grow (mirror of `add_family_member`; idempotent), vs whole-re-put `put_community`.
  - 3-backend parity (pg/sqlite/memory) + FFI for each + thin `Engine` wrappers.

### Added — Cut C (emit ceremonies): `delegates_to` / moderation typed conveniences (CIRISPersist#249)

The **#249 Cut C** typed emit ceremonies — the high-level, signer-based conveniences consumers (form-server, node) hand-roll today, each **composing the #248 `emit_attestation` primitive** (none re-hand-rolls the canonicalize→sign→assemble→`put` recipe; all inherit the #247 derived-key_id floor — attester/scrub is always the signer's DERIVED federation key_id, never a caller alias). Backend-agnostic (emit composes `put_attestation`); verify v6.6.0 inherited from v9.2.2; no version bump.

- **Moderate-scope constants** — `delegation_scope::SCOPE_MODERATE` / `SCOPE_TAKEDOWN` / `SCOPE_REVIEW` (`src/federation/types.rs`), the producer-side names for the §11.10 moderation duties. Each **aliases the `admission::DELEGATION_SCOPE_*` constant BY VALUE** (`"moderate"` / `"takedown"` / `"review"`) — the exact tokens the admission duty-walk's scope-containment check matches — so an edge stamped with one is admissible by `is_named_moderator` / `check_moderation_admission`. A test pins the alias equality.
- **General envelope builder** — `federation::delegates_to_envelope(delegate, scopes, sub_delegation)` (`src/federation/self_at_login.rs`, re-exported from `federation`): emits `scope` as an array-set + a top-level `sub_delegation` bool — the §11.10-admissible shape (the login-specific `delegates_to_agent_envelope` is the §8.1.12.7 specialization).
- **`Engine` ceremonies** (each `#[cfg(postgres|sqlite)]`, composing `emit_attestation`):
  - **`grant_delegation(signer, delegate, scopes, sub_delegation) -> id`** — the general primitive: a `delegates_to` edge keyed by its recipient (`attested_key_id = delegate`, required so the duty walk + `is_owner_bound` retraction-bucketing match the edge / its later withdraws by recipient).
  - **`owner_bind(signer, node_or_agent, infra_scopes) -> id`** — `grant_delegation` with `infra:*`-only scopes (`sub_delegation=false`); passes the CC 4.4.3.4.3 node-agency gate on a node-only key, and afterward `is_owner_bound(node)` holds.
  - **`add_moderator(signer, community, moderator, duty) -> id`** — `grant_delegation` with the single `duty` scope (`sub_delegation=true`); `community` rides the appointment **implicitly** (the §11.10 walk binds a moderator to a community by reaching it from the community's owner-bound authority roots, not via a `community_id` edge field). After it, `is_named_moderator(moderator, community, duty)` holds **iff the signer is an owner-bound community authority** (the caller owns that membership; this helper emits the edge).
  - **`revoke_delegation(signer, target_attestation_id, delegate) -> id`** / **`remove_moderator(signer, community, target_attestation_id, moderator, duty) -> id`** — emit a `withdraws` against the prior `delegates_to`, keyed by the revoked edge's recipient (`attested_key_id`) so the §11.10 walk's per-edge retraction bucketing invalidates it. Admitted as a **producer self-revocation** (withdraws rule 1) when the signer is the original granter.
  - **`file_moderation(signer, content_sha256, community, duty, allegation_type) -> id`** — a `scores` on the `moderation:{allegation_type}:v1` dimension over content; admitted by the always-present `check_delegated_duty_scores_admission` gate when the signer is a `moderate` duty-holder. **Feature-free** (no `--features cirisnode`): the moderation-report **image** is a federation-tier `scores` attestation through the unconditional `emit_attestation` path; the `cirisnode`-gated surface (the `ModerationEvent` put-path / takedown handler) is the SEPARATE node-server ingest path, untouched here.
- **FFI** — `PyEngine.{grant_delegation, owner_bind, add_moderator, revoke_delegation, remove_moderator, file_moderation}` in a labeled `// ── #249 Cut C ──` section, each reconstructing a hybrid-capable Engine over the shared backend + the engine's configured local signer (the #248 `emit_attestation` FFI shape) via a shared `cut_c_emit_handles` helper.
- **Tests** — sqlite + live-Postgres round-trips: `grant_delegation` stores the edge under the derived key_id; `owner_bind` infra:* passes the node-agency gate + owner-binds (with an `agency:*`-rejected negative control); the **`add_moderator` ↔ `is_named_moderator` round-trip** (true after appoint, false after `remove_moderator`); `file_moderation` stores the `moderation:{allegation}:v1` scores row.

## [9.2.0] — 2026-06-19

### Added — `EncryptedKVStore` app-layer XChaCha20-Poly1305 store (CIRISPersist#243 part 3)

- **`EncryptedKVStore` trait + `XChaChaKvStore` impl** (`src/encrypted_kv.rs`, behind the new `encrypted-kv` feature) — a sovereign/edge **encrypted local key/value box** for the openmls `StorageProvider` cold-state CIRISEdge layers on top. Async surface mirrors the `BlobStorage` trait style (`impl Future<Output = …> + Send`): `get(ns, key)` / `put(ns, key, value)` / `delete(ns, key)` / `scan(ns, prefix)`. Typed `KVError` (`WrongPassphrase` / `AuthFailure` / `Crypto` / `Backend` / `InvalidArgument`).
- **Cold-state opacity via app-layer AEAD over the existing bundled rusqlite** — **NOT SQLCipher.** Operator-ratified to **avoid the cross-platform C-build risk**: SQLCipher (or `bundled-sqlcipher`) would change the shared `libsqlite3-sys` across all 7 wheel platforms. Instead the store seals at the application layer with the CIRISVerify **v6.3.0** scope-privacy crypto — pure-Rust `chacha20poly1305` / `hmac` / `hkdf` (**zero new C dependency, no change to the shared bundled rusqlite, no wheel risk**). A dedicated rusqlite DB file (its own `Connection`, `Arc<Mutex<…>>` + `spawn_blocking`, mirroring `SqliteBackend`); self-creates its `encrypted_kv` table (no refinery migration — standalone local store, not the versioned federation schema).
  - **On disk:** value = `xchacha::seal(K_value(ns), nonce=CSPRNG24, value)`; keys **blinded** as `key_blind = HMAC-SHA3-256(K_blind, ns ‖ key)` and `ns_blind = HMAC-SHA3-256(K_blind, ns)`; a **sealed copy of the plaintext key** (`key_ct`) is stored so `scan(prefix)` can recover + prefix-filter plaintext keys (blinded keys aren't prefix-queryable). **No plaintext namespace, key, or value byte ever touches the file** — verified by a load-bearing test (below).
  - **Key hierarchy from the boot passphrase** (HKDF-SHA3-256 / HMAC-SHA3-256, `ciris_crypto::kdf::hkdf_sha3_256` / `ciris_crypto::hmac::sha3_256` / `ciris_crypto::xchacha::{seal,open}`): `root = HKDF(salt=fixed_app_salt, ikm=passphrase, info=".../root/v1")`; `K_blind = HKDF(salt=root, ikm=[], info=".../blind/v1")`; `K_value(ns) = HKDF(salt=root, ikm=ns_bytes, info=".../value/v1")`. `K_value` is **namespace-bound** (namespace = HKDF `ikm`) so namespace isolation is cryptographic, not just a `WHERE` clause. Derived keys + passphrase copy are zeroized on drop.
  - **Boot UX — refuse-to-open-without + wrong-passphrase fail-fast (FSD §7.8 phone-class degraded posture):** on first open the store write-once seals a known constant under a reserved `__verifier__` row (at fixed, passphrase-independent blinds); on subsequent opens a wrong passphrase derives a different `K_value(__verifier__)` ⇒ the AEAD open fails its Poly1305 tag ⇒ `KVError::WrongPassphrase` and the store **refuses to operate** (never silently starts with a bad key). The hardware-key custodian (TPM / Secure Enclave / DPAPI / libsecret *releasing* the passphrase) is the **caller/operator's** responsibility — persist takes the passphrase in (`&[u8]`).
- **Feature wiring:** `encrypted-kv = ["sqlite", "ciris-crypto/kdf", "ciris-crypto/hmac", "ciris-crypto/xchacha", "ciris-crypto/random"]` (pure-Rust verify crypto; no C dep). Added to the `[tool.maturin]` wheel feature list so CIRISEdge gets it. Verify pin **unchanged** (stays v6.3.0). Module is `#[cfg(feature = "encrypted-kv")]`.
- **Tests prove the security property:** get/put/delete roundtrip (bytes exact, incl. empty + full 0..=255 binary); overwrite; delete-then-get→None; `scan(prefix)` plaintext prefix-filtering; **namespace isolation** (a key in ns `a` invisible in ns `b`); **wrong passphrase → open fails** (the refuse-to-start guard); and the load-bearing **COLD-STATE OPACITY** test — write a known plaintext key+value, close, read the raw DB file bytes off disk and assert the plaintext value, key, AND namespace bytes do **not** appear anywhere (only ciphertext). A criterion bench (`benches/encrypted_kv.rs`) reports cold-boot open + per-op overhead vs a plaintext rusqlite baseline.
- **Scope:** part 3 ONLY. Part 4 cohort-lattice contraction remains **BLOCKED** on CIRISRegistry **CEG §11** ratification; **#243 stays open**.

## [9.1.0] — 2026-06-19

### Added — scope-native-privacy blob admission (CC 1.13.3 anonymous-tier; CIRISPersist#243 parts 1+2)

- **`BlobStorage::put_scope_blob` + a read path + LRU eviction** (FSD §2.4 symbol-AEAD store). The substrate half of [CEWP `FSD/SCOPE_PRIVACY.md`](https://github.com/CIRISAI/CEWP/blob/main/FSD/SCOPE_PRIVACY.md) — the CIRIS Constitution **CC 1.13.3** anonymous-tier opt-in mechanism. New table `federation_scope_blobs` (migration **V088**, both dialects) holds caller-pre-encrypted (XChaCha20-Poly1305) RaptorQ symbols at community/family/self scope, addressed by `(record_id, symbol_index)` (the PK; `record_id` = FSD §2.4 HMAC-SHA3-256 output, `symbol_index` = `0..N`, N=20 default).
  - **persist stores opaque ciphertext only.** The seal (`nonce` / `ciphertext` / `tag`) and the `record_id` / `symbol_key` derivation are entirely **CIRISEdge-side** (the producer side is the CIRISVerify **v6.3.0** scope-privacy crypto — HKDF-SHA3 / HMAC-SHA3 / XChaCha20-Poly1305 / X-Wing HPKE; persist consumes none of it). **The scope-blob admission path itself has ZERO verify-crypto dependency** — but this is the cascade's "second cut", so it also re-pins verify to v6.3.0 (below) and CIRISEdge pins one coherent release.
  - **Distinct from `put_blob_signing`:** NO trust-score lookup, NO `attesting_key_id`, NO `AdmissionGate` — holder identity is opaque to outsiders (FSD §2.4) and community-scope eviction is pure **LRU + capacity (CC 1.2)**, never trust-weighted (#243 §1). First-write-wins idempotency on `(record_id, symbol_index)`.
  - `GroupDekRef { community_key_id, epoch }` ties a symbol to the community DEK epoch it was sealed under (resolved from the existing `community_dek_current_epoch` surface); only the epoch is persisted (`group_dek_epoch`) — opaque-holder property.
  - **Read path:** `get_scope_blob` / `list_scope_blob_symbols` (bytes round-trip; reads bump `last_accessed_at`, the LRU signal). **Eviction:** `evict_scope_blobs(max_symbols)` deletes the coldest (oldest `last_accessed_at`) symbols beyond the capacity bound — a parallel LRU sweeper mirroring the `federation_blobs` V053 `(last_accessed_at ASC)` index discipline (no decay scoring, no trust-weighting).
  - **3-backend parity:** trait method on the two at-rest backends (Postgres + SQLite); a degraded-but-present in-memory surface on `MemoryBackend` (inherent methods, mirroring how memory already carries community-DEK rotation *state* while its crypto half is BlobStorage-only). No pg/sqlite asymmetry.
